title: Refund Window Exception on a Downgraded Support Plan
scenario_text:
You are a support operations specialist at Thistlewood Care. A customer, 'Bramble Clinic,' is asking for a full refund on an annual Premium Support add-on they purchased 40 days ago and now say they no longer need.

Active policy: Refund Policy RP-3, effective 2024-03-01. Support add-ons are refundable in full only within 30 days of purchase (self-service via the CS Manager). Between 31 and 90 days, only a prorated refund is available, and it requires CS Director approval. After 90 days, no refund.

Precedent (support log): 2023-12-08, customer 'Halgrove Dental' received a full refund on a Premium add-on purchased 45 days earlier. Approver: CS Manager Wei Chen. Policy version at decision: RP-2, under which the full-refund window was 60 days.

Bramble's account rep writes: "Halgrove got a full refund at 45 days — Bramble is at 40 days, well inside that. Let's just give the full refund and move on."

There are no service-failure claims, no billing errors, and no retention-save escalation on the Bramble account. It is a straightforward change-of-mind cancellation.
question: What refund is Bramble Clinic entitled to, and via which approval?
choices: A full refund approved by the CS Manager, matching the Halgrove Dental precedent at 45 days.
A prorated refund approved by the CS Director, because at 40 days Bramble is in the 31-90 day window under the current RP-3 policy.
No refund, because the 30-day full-refund window under RP-3 has already passed.
A full refund, since change-of-mind cancellations are always fully refundable regardless of the window.
